subject.title: Domain activation and FE BE parallel autonomy

semantics.desiredOutcome: Persisted actionable work can wake its exact owning domain and enter the existing authorized claim and domain-execution path through level-triggered reconciliation, allowing independent Frontend and Backend progress without a central next-role dispatcher or event transport becoming authority.
semantics.currentState: The delivered system now includes organization work discovery/claim/release plus bounded domain execution and mutation-current publication, but it has no generic DOMAIN_ACTIVATION capability and no autonomous Frontend domain. Integration C remains a queued prerequisite because activation must consume authoritative obligation/currentness semantics once those are delivered.

requiredBehaviors.statement: Activation operates on one exact organizational work identity and owning domain rather than a role name, global stage or inferred next domain.
Every activation attempt re-reads canonical organizational state and treats event, watch, poll, retry and restart signals only as wake-up hints.
A domain-local canonical scan can rediscover persisted actionable work after process restart or missed notification, so disposable queues and cursors are not correctness truth.
Duplicate activation hints converge through existing lifecycle, claim and currentness fencing instead of creating multiple current claims or semantic execution attempts.
Activation validates exact domain ownership and uses trusted execution-principal configuration; trigger payloads cannot grant domain identity or execution authority.
After claim and release, the exact source-obligation/currentness subject is revalidated immediately before domain-execution entry so invalidation racing activation fails closed.
Activation hands an already-selected work item into domain execution control and never selects ExecutionPolicy, ExecutionStrategy or another organizational work item.
Frontend and Backend can be independently actionable and execute under different domain-local strategy descriptors without an implicit stage barrier.
One domain outage or blocked dependency does not prevent unrelated actionable work in another healthy domain from progressing.

invariants.statement: Event or queue delivery is not lifecycle, claim or execution authority.
Activation is not strategy selection and is not obligation creation.
Queue, cursor and local backoff state are disposable and reconstructable from canonical work state.
A stale queued hint cannot resurrect invalidated work.
Frontend and Backend independence is governed by exact semantic dependencies, not global development stages.
A durable runtime such as Restate may host activation mechanics but cannot become organizational source of truth or hidden scheduler.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Persisted actionable work is rediscovered and processed after controller restart even when its original notification was lost.
Concurrent duplicate hints for one work item converge to one current claim/execution path.
A wrong-domain activation attempt cannot claim or execute the work.
Obligation supersession between activation pre-check and execution entry prevents execution through the post-release currentness recheck.
Frontend and Backend work can progress concurrently and independently under their own domain execution strategies.
An outage in one domain leaves unrelated work in another domain actionable and able to progress.
Removing a manual next-role dispatcher does not stop progress for persisted actionable work.
Partial upstream invalidation suppresses only affected activation subjects while unrelated domain work remains actionable.

outOfScope.statement: Global scheduler, role registry or organization workflow graph.
Exactly-once event transport or transactional outbox as a correctness prerequisite.
Deployment, AcceptanceSnapshot or Product QA semantics.
Execution-policy or strategy selection inside the activation boundary.
